## Context

- `map_handler_return` in `src/dispatch.rs` handles plain `str`/`bytes` on the hot path.
- `PyString` → `to_string().into_bytes()`; `PyBytes` → `as_bytes().to_vec()` before `protocol.response_bytes`.

## Problem

Every plain-text or binary response copies data at least once into an owned `Vec<u8>` even when the handler already returned an immutable buffer.

## Proposed change

- Investigate Granian RSGI protocol APIs and PyO3 buffer handling.
- Where safe, pass `PyBytes` or borrowed bytes to the protocol without an intermediate `Vec<u8>`, or reduce copies to a single guaranteed copy.
- Apply the same principle to sync fast-path send helpers in `src/response.rs`.

## Files

- `src/dispatch.rs`, `src/response.rs`
- tests for `str`/`bytes` responses and HEAD `Content-Length`

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing response mapping tests pass.
- HEAD responses preserve correct `Content-Length`.
- Benchmark or allocation profile shows reduced copies on bytes-heavy routes.

## Expected low-level impact

Less memory bandwidth and heap pressure on static/binary/plain responses.
